title: How do seahorses swim upright?
examples: Why do seahorses hold on with their tails?

forces.label: Upthrust
forces.ask: How does a seahorse go up and down?

explain.say: Seahorses are fish, but they swim standing upright with their heads bent forward. They are among the slowest swimmers in the sea.

forces.label: Upthrust
forces.ask: How does a seahorse go up and down?

explain.say: A seahorse moves by fluttering the small fin on its back, the dorsal fin, dozens of times a second. Tiny pectoral fins behind its head steer it.

forces.label: Upthrust
forces.ask: How does a seahorse go up and down?

explain.say: A swim bladder controls its height. By changing the gas inside, the seahorse rises or sinks, and because the bladder runs along its upright body, it stays standing.

forces.label: Upthrust
forces.ask: How does a seahorse go up and down?

explain.say: Being slow matters little, because a seahorse spends most of its time anchored by its gripping tail to seagrass or coral, snapping up tiny shrimp that drift past with a lightning flick of its snout.

faq.a: Seahorses push themselves along by fluttering the dorsal fin on their back very fast, and steer with two small pectoral fins near the head. They swim upright and slowly.
asks: What fin does a seahorse use?

faq.q: How does a seahorse go up and down?
faq.a: It changes the amount of gas in its swim bladder. More gas makes it rise, less makes it sink, and the shape of the bladder keeps it upright.
asks: Do seahorses have a swim bladder?

faq.q: Why do seahorses hold on with their tails?
faq.a: Seahorses are weak swimmers, so they wrap their tail around seagrass or coral to avoid being swept away and wait for food to drift past. Their tail is square in cross-section, which makes it grip well and resist crushing.
asks: What is a seahorse tail for?

faq.a: The dwarf seahorse is often named the slowest fish, with a top speed of only about 1.5 metres per hour.

faq.q: Is a seahorse really a fish?
faq.a: Yes. A seahorse has gills, fins and a swim bladder, though instead of scales its body is covered in bony plates. Unusually, the male carries the eggs in a pouch until they hatch.
asks: Why is a seahorse a fish?

facts: The dwarf seahorse's top speed is about 1.5 metres per hour.
Seahorse tails are square in cross-section, which makes them grip well and resist crushing (Porter and colleagues, 2015).

quiz.say: Which fin mainly pushes a seahorse along?
quiz.show: Which fin mainly pushes a seahorse along?

options.show: The dorsal fin on its back
options.say: The dorsal fin on its back

quiz.why: The fluttering dorsal fin provides the thrust, while the pectoral fins steer.

wrong.1: Seahorses have no tail fin; the tail is for gripping.
wrong.2: Gill covers protect the gills; they do not push.

quiz.say: Why can a seahorse survive being such a slow swimmer?
quiz.show: Why can a seahorse survive being such a slow swimmer?

options.show: It anchors with its tail and waits for food
options.say: It anchors with its tail and waits for food

quiz.why: Gripping seagrass or coral, it lets tiny shrimp drift to it and snaps them up.

wrong.1: Seahorses eat tiny animals such as shrimp.
wrong.2: Seahorses live in the sea, often in currents.
